audit.why: 54.77% over 1028 games at 6/10. Swain has no dash and no escape; every level before his soul stacks matter belongs to a champion with three mobility casts.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four level-chart rows disagree with the packet chart, three of them contradicting their own why-text. Packet is [Riven, Riven, Riven, Riven, Riven, Riven, Skill]; both layers hold [Skill, Riven, Riven, Skill, Skill, Riven, Riven].
audit.why: whys[0] says 'he has no root or drain yet to respond with' under win[0]=Skill. whys[3] says 'Your short-trade pattern beats his sustained drain kit at Levels 4-5' under win[3]=Skill. whys[4] says Blade of the Exile 'outpace[s] his Level 6 R drain ramp' under win[4]=Skill. And win[6]=Riven sits over a whys[6] that describes a soul-stacked Swain as a burst check you cannot pass.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 3, 4 -> Riven; row 6 -> Skill, in both layers, with ratings re-pointed and phases[6].why rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nevermove is taught as a thing you dodge on the way out. Riot's text: 'Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It THEN RETURNS to Swain and roots enemies it hits.' The outgoing wave does nothing — the root is on the return pass. content.early ('sidestep his E or dash through it with E-Valor') and spikes[2].text both describe dodging the harmless half.
audit.why: Dashing through the outgoing wave is not counterplay; it puts you exactly where the return sweeps. The correct read is to be clear of the line when it comes back to him, which is also why his 12-second E is a real punish window rather than a coin flip. Second interaction the page misses entirely: Death's Hand fires SEVERAL bolts that pierce, and 'Enemies hit take more damage for each bolt they are struck by' — so standing point-blank on Swain, which Riven must do, stacks his own poke onto her.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text rewritten onto the return-pass root; whys[0] rewritten to name Death's Hand and its distance-scaling bolt stack.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both flagged missing interactions are absent from the content layer: Ravenous Flock heals him and PERMANENTLY increases his maximum health, and neither Grievous Wounds nor the futility of raw resistances is mentioned anywhere outside a single encoding-damaged report line.
audit.why: Anti-heal is the difference between a won all-in and a Swain who walks away full. His health also grows across the game independent of items, so the 'he has no AP yet' framing in whys[5] undersells why the early kill matters.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds and Ravenous Flock written into content.mid and whys[6].

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet defect is real: outside the repeated 'Demonic Ascension' in the full layer, the page never names Ravenous Flock, Death's Hand, Vision of Empire or Nevermove — it says 'his E pull', 'his W bomb', 'Q poke'.
audit.why: The user's approved bar names the ability. 'Root you with the returning Nevermove inside Vision of Empire' is checkable; 'land his E pull inside his W circle' is not.
audit.corrected: All four names introduced across whys[0], whys[6], spikes[2].text and wants.foe[0].

edits.after: Nevermove roots on the RETURN pass, not on the way out — crossing the outgoing wave costs nothing; you have to be clear of the line when it sweeps back to him.

edits.after: Root you with the returning Nevermove inside Vision of Empire, then open Demonic Ascension

edits.before: With your early lead established, Swain's Level 6 R drain becomes his last realistic comeback tool — the plan is to never let it run long enough to matter. When he activates R, his drain is powerful in a sustained fight but your combo window is faster than his ramp: E in, W-stun him immediately to interrupt his ability to position and drain, then burn the full Q chain and execute with Wind Slash before he heals more than one or two drain ticks. Your Blade of the Exile also extends your melee range, keeping you inside his W bomb whether he likes it or not — he cannot kite your extended Q3 the way he kites shorter-ranged melee. If you are ahead, shove the wave and roam mid at Level 6; Swain has no mobility to follow, and you convert your lane lead into a global one before his soul stacks make him relevant in team fights.
edits.after: With your early lead established, Demonic Ascension becomes his last realistic comeback tool — the plan is to never let it run long enough to matter. It is 120 seconds flat and stays up only while he drains a champion, so deny him the target: E in, W-stun him immediately, then burn the full Q chain and Wind Slash him. Bring Grievous Wounds, because Ravenous Flock heals him and permanently grows his maximum health every fight you let him survive. Blade of the Exile also extends your range, keeping you inside Vision of Empire whether he likes it or not — he cannot kite your extended Q3. If you are ahead, shove and roam mid at 6; Swain has no dash to follow, and you convert the lane lead before his soul stacks matter.

notes: The biggest correction here is Nevermove: the page told the player twice to dash through the E, when the outgoing wave is harmless and the root lands on the return sweep — following that advice puts you exactly where the root catches you. Also worth noting for the wider run: Riven's own R is flagged 'projectile' in her kit, meaning Wind Slash is Wind Wall / spell-shield blockable. Swain has neither, so it does not apply here, but several of my remaining matchups may.
